forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - St Annes Seawall - Design Development Fully Funded Budget Increase
findings.headline: The design phase does not commit the council to construction; any future build decision will require separate funding approval
findings.detail: The paper explicitly states the design work does not commit the council to the construction phase, with any future construction decision requiring a separate report, confirmation of funding, and governance approval. This represents a staged approach where the council will assess final costs and programme before deciding whether to proceed.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether this £400k is precursor to a much larger capital commitment; the council is explicitly retaining flexibility on the next phase.
findings.quote: The detailed design work does not commit the Council to the future construction phase. Any future decision to proceed with construction will be subject to a separate report, confirmation of funding and approval through the Council's governance processes.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - St Annes Seawall - Design Development Fully Funded Budget Increase
findings.headline: The design phase is entirely externally funded, protecting reserves that the 2021 decision had allocated to the now-cancelled scheme
findings.detail: The 2021 decision approved £2.3m from the Funding Volatility Reserve for the original seawall scheme, phased 2021/22 to 2024/25. The new design phase is stated to be 'fully funded via the Environment Agency's Regional Area Programme Delivery Mandate', with no council capital contribution at this stage.
findings.matters: The original scheme would have materially drawn on council reserves during a period of wider financial pressure; the externally-funded design phase preserves that reserve capacity.
findings.quote: To approve a new capital scheme addition of £400,000 within the Capital Programme for 2026/27 to fund the St Annes Seawall Detailed Design Project , fully funded via the Environment Agency's Regional Area Programme Delivery Mandate.

findings.paper_title: Item 9 - St Annes Seawall - Design Development Fully Funded Budget Increase
findings.headline: A seawall scheme rejected in 2023 due to cost escalation is being reactivated at design stage with a different technical approach and external funding
findings.detail: Fylde rejected a £11.82m seawall replacement project in October 2023 due to 'significant cost increases' and risk of business disruption costs. The council is now approving a £400,000 design phase for a revised approach using concrete overlay repair rather than replacement, intended to provide 100 years of protection before adaptive raising is required.
findings.matters: It shows how the council is managing a strategic coastal infrastructure challenge after an earlier project cancellation, revealing whether the asset risk has been resolved or deferred.
findings.quote: It was RESOLVED to not proceed with procurement and delivery of the St Annes Seawall capital scheme due to significant cost increases identified as part of the detailed design work undertaken to date, and the significant risk of potential business disruption costs exceeding their budget allocation.

findings.paper_title: Item 6 - Appendix 1 - MIAA Internal Audit Progress Report September 2026
findings.headline: Limited Assurance on building statutory compliance with critical and high-priority recommendations
findings.detail: Statutory Compliance – Buildings audit finalised with Limited Assurance. Significant control gaps remain in asbestos surveys, fire risk assessments, and statutory inspection policies following the transfer of building maintenance to Blackpool Council in September 2025. The audit found incomplete records, lack of documented policies for fire, gas and electrical inspections, misalignment between service level agreements and actual inspection frequencies, and absence of performance reporting on the outsourced service. Although legionnaires testing is being completed monthly, key gaps in statutory records and inspections remain across the estate.
findings.matters: Gaps in mandatory building compliance create direct legal, financial, health-and-safety, and reputational risks; a lender needs assurance that material obligations and liabilities are being identified and managed.
findings.figures: Limited Assurance rating; 1 Critical, 1 High, 4 Medium, 1 Low recommendations; 7 remedial actions not yet due as at 9 September 2026
findings.quote: If the council does not undertake Asbestos Surveys and Fire Risk Assessments in accordance with statutory requirements, the implications are significant from a health and safety, legal, financial, operational, and reputational perspective.

findings.paper_title: Item 4 - KPMG External Audit Plan and Strategy 2025-26
findings.headline: No significant risks identified in Financial Sustainability, Governance, or Economy.
findings.detail: KPMG's Value for Money assessment identified no significant risks in three domains: Financial Sustainability, Governance, and Improving Economy, Efficiency and Effectiveness. This is the auditors' initial risk assessment ahead of their full audit and opinion.
findings.matters: An external auditor's finding of no significant risks in financial sustainability and governance provides independent assurance on the council's financial management and control environment, which directly informs lender confidence in financial stability.
findings.quote: no significant risks have been identified regarding the measures the council has in place for each of the three relevant domains covered by the Value for Money assessment, namely Financial Sustainability, Governance, and Improving Economy, Efficiency and Effectiveness
